messages:
Evelyn: Short sync: propose we split the admit probe into sampler (what to pick) and orchestrator (how to run). tradeoffs?

Ajay: +1. Sampling will iterate fast; orchestration should be stable and focus on backpressure/retries.

Leah: Agree. Sampling must guarantee stratification so we don't miss regressions from biased picks.

Tom: Keep a tiny contract: sampler -> BatchDescriptor, orchestrator.run(BatchDescriptor) -> ResultBundle. Minimal surface.

Evelyn: BatchDescriptor fields I'd expect: id, payload_uri, features(seqlen,tokens), hints(priority,timeout,force_fresh_kv), provenance(policy_id,sampler_version), fingerprint.

Ravi: Golden samples need stronger invariants: fixed seed, no caching. Orchestrator should obey hints not invent them.

Ajay: Orchestrator should expose tiered queues (smoke/full/golden) and per-tier capacity to avoid long benches starving smoke runs.

Leah: Observability: sampler emits selection weights + histograms; orchestrator emits queue depths, runtimes, failure reasons, GPU tags. Link via batch_id.

Tom: Failure modes: OOM -> try quantized fallback or route to offline slowpath and mark sample flaky. Emit "needs-profile" back to sampler.

Evelyn: Deployment modes: hosted | dedicated | private. For private, payloads must be local-only. BatchDescriptor should include deployment_mode.

Ravi: Centralized sampler policy gives global coverage but is a single change risk. Hybrid approach: central policy controller + local cached samplers that can operate if controller is down.

benchbot: policy-rollout detected: sampler v2.8 -> v2.9; dist-delta {short:+3.7%, long:-2.9%}.

Leah: Rollouts need a shadow window with diff summaries before flipping. I'll own sampler PoC (central policy + local cache).

Ajay: I'll prototype orchestrator queues and hint handling.

Evelyn: I'll draft RFC with API contracts, sample lifecycle, and failure handling and link this thread. Thanks.
